issue_paraphrase: Decrypting with the PSA crypto API using AES in CCM* mode without a separate tag rejects short but perfectly valid messages. When the nonce-plus-ciphertext input is shorter than one AES block (16 bytes), the call fails with an invalid-argument error even though CCM* only needs the input to be at least as long as the nonce it is given. A ciphertext of 2 bytes or even 0 bytes after the nonce is rejected, while the identical message a couple of bytes longer decrypts fine, so saved or relayed packets of 1-3 bytes are spuriously dropped.
fix_summary: psa_cipher_decrypt() had a special-case error check that rejected any CCM*-without-tag input shorter than one cipher block (16 bytes for AES), on top of the generic check that enforces the nonce/IV length (13 bytes for CCM*). The fix deletes the block-size special case and keeps only the IV-length check, so decrypting a message as short as the nonce length works.
notes: Default config enables MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C and PSA_WANT_ALG_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG so the new tests are compiled in. The suite runs in a few seconds once built; library build ~2 min at -j8 (~15-20 min at 1 CPU). All other 1947 suite cases pass at the parent, so any failure is unambiguous. The eventual task image must pin the framework submodule (git submodule update --init framework) and use the https apt rewrite; both observed in this run.

install_recipe: apt-get update with https:// rewritten in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources (plain http is blocked on this host); DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y build-essential perl python3 python3-jsonschema python3-jinja2 cmake; git config --global --add safe.directory '*'; git submodule update --init framework; git -C tf-psa-crypto submodule update --init framework; cmake -B build -DENABLE_TESTING=ON .; cmake --build build --target test_suite_pkcs7 -j8
issue_paraphrase: An application that reuses the same PKCS#7 structure object to parse a second message after freeing the first one crashes with a double free. The parser's cleanup routine only nulls one internal field, so the linked list of signer records still points at memory that has already been handed back; parsing a follow-up message that carries no signers leaves that stale link in place, and the next cleanup attempt frees the same record twice. The library aborts the whole process with a glibc double-free error instead of parsing the new message.
fix_summary: mbedtls_pkcs7_free() previously set only pkcs7->raw.p = NULL after releasing the certificate/CRL and signer records, leaving the signer linked list and other fields as dangling pointers. The fix replaces that with mbedtls_platform_zeroize() over the whole mbedtls_pkcs7 structure so the object is cleanly reinitialized and safe to parse into again.
notes: Default config enables MBEDTLS_PKCS7_C and MBEDTLS_FS_IO so the new test compiles and runs. The double-free abort is deterministic (glibc tcache check) in the Ubuntu 24.04 toolchain. The two framework checkouts (top-level and nested inside tf-psa-crypto) are mandatory for configure to succeed ('framework/CMakeLists.txt not found' otherwise). Suite build is a few minutes at -j8; the suite itself runs in seconds.

install_recipe: apt-get update with https:// rewritten in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources (plain http is blocked on this host); DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y build-essential perl python3 python3-jsonschema python3-jinja2; git config --global --add safe.directory '*'; git submodule update --init framework; make -j8 lib; make -C tests test_suite_psa_crypto_util
issue_paraphrase: Converting ECDSA signatures between the raw (r||s) and DER (ASN.1) encodings crashes or corrupts memory when the caller supplies a curve bit size larger than the biggest curve the library supports (521 bits). The conversion routine copies each coordinate into a fixed-size internal stack buffer that only fits the largest supported curve, without checking the size of the incoming value, so a 544-bit value overflows the buffer. On hardened glibc builds the process is aborted with a buffer-overflow error; without that protection the stack is silently corrupted and the routine returns a misleading status or crashes later.
fix_summary: mbedtls_ecdsa_raw_to_der() and mbedtls_ecdsa_der_to_raw() now verify that the coordinate length (PSA_BITS_TO_BYTES(bits)) fits their fixed-size local buffers (MBEDTLS_ECP_MAX_BYTES) before copying, returning MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_BUF_TOO_SMALL instead of overflowing the stack.
notes: Security fix (CVE-2024-45157): the advisory title itself hints at the two functions, so the paraphrase above deliberately omits the function names. The test cases have no depends_on guard, so they always run; the rest of the suite (43 cases) passes untouched. Suite compiles in under a minute and runs in seconds; library build is the long pole (~2 min at -j8, ~15-20 min at 1 CPU). Fail-at-parent is deterministic on Ubuntu 24.04 gcc due to FORTIFY_SOURCE.
